title: Using economic impact evidence to get into the rooms that matter
gist: Promotional Oxford Economics webinar (1 Dec 2026) pitching that quantifying a company's economic footprint — supply-chain jobs, output and tax revenues — earns access to local policymakers, and introducing new online impact-measurement tools. Thin, promotional content.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics argues local decision-makers listen to businesses they see as mattering to their economies, so quantifying a company's supported supply-chain jobs, output and stimulated tax revenues helps it gain access to policy decisions.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Corporate affairs teams increasingly buy economic-footprint studies as lobbying evidence — a niche but growing consulting product.
insights.quote: Local decision-makers listen to the businesses they see as mattering to their economies.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics is introducing new online tools that let businesses measure their economic contribution consistently and quickly, productizing what was previously bespoke economic-impact consulting.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Shift from bespoke studies to self-service calculators signals commoditization of economic-impact consulting.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics' economic-footprint team has run global economic impact studies for the beer and tourism sectors and footprint assessments for the European Space Agency, Rolls-Royce, Boeing and Huawei.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Large aerospace and tech firms use footprint studies to support their political standing in Europe.
